decisions.reason: Cocos nucifera at 70 cm is a confirmed non-native species obstructing the footprint. Statutory compensation is 21-58 saplings, identical to what a native of the same girth would require — but the recommended mix is native-weighted, so the replanting is not simply more Subabul.
decisions.statutory_basis: Maharashtra (Urban Areas) Protection of Trees Act 1975, s.7 — compensation is age-equivalent and SPECIES-BLIND. The statutory count is identical for a native and a non-native tree. This tool applies the same count to both and expresses the native/non-native distinction in the recommended species mix instead, which is the ecologically meaningful lever and stays inside the Act.

recommendations.action: Reduce impervious cover by 18 percentage points (permeable paving, green roof, or open landscape)
Substitute 35% of each material with its lower-carbon alternative
Redesign the footprint to retain the 4 heritage-class trees on site, recovering 96 m2 of canopy
recommendations.composite_tradeoff: green 97.1 -> 96.2 (improves by 0.9), but carbon intensity rises 13.2 -> 14.3 because the same materials are spread over a smaller footprint. Composite impact moves +0.1.
recommendations.note: Canopy preserved rather than replaced. Saplings do not substitute for retained mature canopy on any useful timescale.
